title: Mathematical Formulation of the Double Pendulum System
system_description: Planar double pendulum: two point masses m1, m2 connected by rigid massless rods of lengths L1, L2. The first rod pivots at a fixed point. Both swing freely in the vertical plane under gravity g.

generalized_coordinates.theta1: Angle of first pendulum rod from vertical (positive counterclockwise)
generalized_coordinates.theta2: Angle of second pendulum rod from vertical (positive counterclockwise)

kinetic_energy: T = (1/2) * (m1 + m2) * L1^2 * dtheta1^2 + (1/2) * m2 * L2^2 * dtheta2^2 + m2 * L1 * L2 * dtheta1 * dtheta2 * cos(theta1 - theta2)
potential_energy: V = -(m1 + m2) * g * L1 * cos(theta1) - m2 * g * L2 * cos(theta2)

euler_lagrange_equations.eq1: (m1 + m2) * L1 * ddtheta1 + m2 * L2 * ddtheta2 * cos(theta1 - theta2) + m2 * L2 * dtheta2^2 * sin(theta1 - theta2) + (m1 + m2) * g * sin(theta1) = 0
euler_lagrange_equations.eq2: m2 * L2 * ddtheta2 + m2 * L1 * ddtheta1 * cos(theta1 - theta2) - m2 * L1 * dtheta1^2 * sin(theta1 - theta2) + m2 * g * sin(theta2) = 0

solved_angular_accelerations.description: Solving the 2x2 linear system for ddtheta1 and ddtheta2. Let delta = theta1 - theta2, M = m1 + m2.
solved_angular_accelerations.ddtheta1: (-m2 * L2 * dtheta2^2 * sin(delta) - M * g * sin(theta1) + m2 * g * sin(theta2) * cos(delta) - m2 * L1 * dtheta1^2 * sin(delta) * cos(delta)) * L2 / den ... (see implementation for exact form)
solved_angular_accelerations.ddtheta2: Symmetric expression (see implementation for exact form)
solved_angular_accelerations.note: The exact expressions are implemented in pendulum.py as the derivatives function, following the Wikipedia double pendulum article formulation.

first_order_system.state_vector: [theta1, omega1, theta2, omega2] where omega1 = dtheta1/dt, omega2 = dtheta2/dt

consistency_check: Equations match Wikipedia double pendulum article and are consistent with Shinbrot et al. 1992 formulation.
